name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.injective_of_singleton
title: Faithfulness from a unique irreducible class

content.display_title: Faithfulness from a unique irreducible class
content.one_sentence_role: Uses a pure state on the unitization to detect any hypothetical nonzero element of the kernel.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ represent the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations of $A$. Then $\pi$ is injective: $$\pi(x)=\pi(y)\Longrightarrow x=y.$$
content.assumptions: No separability of $A$ or $H$ is required. Faithfulness of the representation of the unitization is neither assumed nor concluded.
content.conclusion: The original representation of $A$ has zero kernel.
content.proof_summary: A nonzero kernel element would be detected in a pure GNS representation of the unitization. Its nonzero irreducible restriction is compared with the given representation, forcing that detected operator to be zero.
proof_steps:
If $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$, put $a=x-y$, so $\pi(a)=0$. Suppose $a
e0$ and let $\iota:A	o\widetilde A$ be the canonical injective inclusion into the complex unitization. Then $\iota(a)
e0$. Apply [Pure-state detection of a nonzero square](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/Faithful.lean#L27-L64) in the nonzero unital ordered $C^*$-algebra $\widetilde A$ to this element. It gives a pure state $\varphi$ with $\varphi(\iota(a)^*\iota(a))
e0$.

Let $(H_\varphi,\rho_U,\xi)$ be its GNS representation with $\|\xi\|=1$. By [Irreducibility of the GNS representation of a pure state](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/State/Irreducible.lean#L127-L144), purity makes $\rho_U$ irreducible. Restrict it to $A$ by $\rho(b)=\rho_U(\iota(b))$. The GNS identity gives $$\|\rho(a)\xi\|^2=\varphi(\iota(a)^*\iota(a))\ne0,$$ so $\rho(a)\ne0$ and the restriction is a nonzero representation.

A closed subspace reducing $\rho(A)$ also reduces all $\rho_U(\lambda,b)=\lambda I+\rho(b)$, and conversely. Thus irreducibility of $\rho_U$, together with the nonzero restriction established in Step 2, gives nonzero irreducibility of $\rho$. This is the restriction criterion applied in the exact proof.

The singleton condition applied to this $\rho$ supplies a unitary $U:H\to H_\varphi$ with $\rho(b)U=U\pi(b)$. Since $U$ is surjective, every $z\in H_\varphi$ equals $Uq$ for some $q\in H$, and $$\rho(a)z=\rho(a)Uq=U\pi(a)q=0.$$ Hence $\rho(a)=0$, contradicting Step 2. Therefore $a=0$ and $x=y$.
